# Remediation Plan

### Step-by-step Mitigation Strategies

#### SQL Injection Prevention
Use prepared statements instead of concatenating raw strings directly with variables. For example, replace:
```c++
char* unsafe_query = malloc(256);
sprintf(unsafe_query, "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=%d;", userid); // UNSAFE!
```
With parameterized queries using PostgreSQL bindings.

#### Buffer Overflow Defense
Employ bounds checking before copying/moving buffers between regions. This ensures no overflow occurs:
```c++
if(strlen(input_data) > MAXLEN){
    return ERROR;
}
memcpy(dest_buffer,input_data,MAXLEN); 
```
Also consider enabling compiler flags (`-fstack-protector`, `-Wformat-security`) to mitigate common errors.

#### Cryptographic Upgrade Recommendations
Switch deprecated MD5 hashes used internally to SHA-2 variants (SHA-256/SHA-512). Add salting techniques to enhance password storage resilience against brute-forcing attempts.

#### Filesystem Protection Measures
Validate file names/path arguments ensuring they're safe prior to invoking IO-read/write ops. Here’s a simplified check:
```c++
bool validate_filepath(const char* fpath){
    if(strstr(fpath,"..") != NULL || strchr(fpath,'/') == NULL)
        return false;
    return true;
}
```
This reduces chances of out-of-bounds directory traversals.

Other measures include frequent dependency updates, static analysis tools integration, stress testing, and continuous monitoring.
